text.insert: ProjectSession is the durable container for the project worktree, head_revision, and the ordered timeline that explains head lineage. Its timeline defines epoch_completed, remote_application, pr_phase, and save_point entries. The session container records epoch_completed and save_point entries, while the PR-campaign and sync workflow contracts own the pr_phase and remote_application writers. Save points anchor evidence to existing commits without creating commits; this page defines their capture, failure, and close-gate semantics.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — head lineage is transactional; save points are evidence anchors

text.insert: ProjectSession owns the worktree and head_revision, and the timeline reserves head movement for epoch_completed and remote_application entries. The session container records epoch_completed and save_point entries; the PR-campaign and sync contracts own pr_phase and remote_application recording.
Why Lineage and Evidence Split

Head movement and evidence capture need different atomicity. The epoch boundary couples its integration commit to epoch_completed recording, and the sync contract assigns the same boundary atomicity to remote_application publication. A save point explains an existing source position with reports, a board snapshot, and the headline score, so it remains cheap and frequent without manufacturing history.
Timeline Responsibilities
The ProjectSession timeline keeps lineage and evidence in one ordered record while applying the failure policy required by each entry class.

rows: epoch_completed
Advances head_revision through an epoch integration commit.
The entry exists if and only if its commit exists; a failed durable step fails the boundary loudly.
remote_application
Defines head_revision advancement through the sync workflow's published remote-application boundary.
The sync workflow contract couples the entry and boundary commit in one atomic publish.
pr_phase
Defines PR-campaign activation and release evidence without advancing head.
The PR-campaign workflow contract owns this writer and its lease-bound phase evidence.
save_point
Anchors reports, the board snapshot, and the headline score to an existing commit.
Failure raises a durable session blocker and staleness flag but does not block the triggering boundary.

text.insert: Save-Point Structure
A save point records enough evidence to reproduce what the project looked like at one existing commit without changing the checkout.

rows: commit_sha / branch
The exact existing checkout position that the evidence describes; recording the save point never creates this commit.
base_ref / base_sha
The upstream anchor, defaulting to origin/master, against which the position is measured.
trigger_kind
The producing boundary: manual, init, pause, checkpoint, epoch, qa, ship, sync, or fresh.
Score and artifacts
matched_code_percent is the headline measure; report copies live under state_dir/save_points/<timestamp>/, and board_snapshot_path identifies the board evidence beside them.
Worktree and payload
worktree_dirty records remaining uncommitted work; payload carries ahead-of-base count, dirty paths, evidence warnings, and full measures.

text.insert: Capture and Failure Semantics

Automatic evidence hooks at init, pause, checkpoint, epoch, QA, ship, sync, and fresh-run boundaries join manual creation through the save-point server job and Save Point dashboard action. The save-point path records evidence at the current commit; it never stages work or creates a commit. Pause, ship, sync, and init boundaries perform their explicit boundary-owned commit first, then invoke save-point capture against the resulting HEAD. Epoch publication likewise establishes its integration commit before its evidence anchor.
A successful hook appends the save_point entry and its evidence to the durable session timeline.
A failed hook raises a durable session blocker and marks the evidence stale, so the failure is visible instead of becoming a silent log line.
The triggering boundary continues after a save-point failure because the hook records evidence rather than head lineage.
Transactional head publication belongs to the epoch boundary and the sync workflow contract, not to save-point capture.
Session Close Gate

Session close treats the current head and its evidence anchor as one gate. The dispatch lease must be free, the worktree must contain no changes beyond head_revision, save-point evidence must be fresh, and the operator must select a named save point whose commit matches head_revision. Ahead-of-base commits may remain because the clean, named anchor makes that session head explicit.
Where-We-Are Contract

The dashboard reads the active ProjectSession and answers where the project stands from durable state without triggering a build. Its session-backed projection combines the canonical head lineage with the most recent evidence anchor:
The latest save point supplies its commit, trigger, matched percent, and artifacts, so every displayed result names the source position it describes.
The current head supplies head_revision, branch, and dirty paths, so the projection can compare live position with the evidence anchor.
aheadOfBase counts commits that have not been merged into the base reference, which is the durable answer to what has not shipped.
stale is true when head moved past the save point, uncommitted changes exist, or save-point capture failed; the UI exposes the stale evidence instead of presenting old numbers as current.
Relationship to Runs and the Ledger

ProjectSession is the durable parent of run, PR, and sync workflows, while runs, target claims, worker states, checkpoints, and report artifacts keep their internal run keys. Each save point records the run active when the evidence was captured. The local change ledger carries patches, facts, and lessons across save points and sessions; only shipped PR candidates leave the system. Reverting to a save point is git-native because its existing commit, reports, and board state travel together.
